title: Bias, Fairness, and Societal Impacts in Biomedical AI
audience: Basic science learners reflecting on bias and fairness in biomedical AI research
objectives: Imagine a useful AI system for biomedical research and identify fairness safeguards.
Analyze vectors of bias in public-health crisis algorithms.
Explain risks from demographic mismatch, income mismatch, and overreliance on algorithmic guidance.
Reflect on how to check for and prevent bias in research collaborations.

sections.name: Ideal AI System for Biomedical Research
sections.purpose: Prompt learners to design a research AI system and anticipate bias.
sections.how_to_use: Describe what the system would do, why it is needed, what data it would use, and how bias would be mitigated.

sections.name: Public Health Crisis Algorithm Case Study
sections.purpose: Analyze bias from nonrepresentative public-health training data.
sections.how_to_use: Read the case and write possible bias vectors, deployment considerations, and negative outcomes.

sections.name: Reflection and Takeaways
sections.purpose: Connect bias and fairness to the learner's own research practice.
sections.how_to_use: Write key takeaways and concrete ways to check or prevent bias in future projects.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, guide the learner through the ideal-system prompt, the case study, and reflection.
For basic science users, emphasize representation, data source mismatch, downstream societal impact, and critical interpretation.
Help learners identify who benefits, who is excluded, and who may be harmed.
